C: › [ C ] an insect in the stage when it has just come out of its egg

I usually + adv/prep: › [ I usually + adv/prep ] to search for something by digging or turning over earth

example: A grub looks like a short, fat worm.
昆蟲的幼蟲看上去像一條又短又粗的軟蟲子。
I'm starving - let's get some grub.
我要餓死了——我們去找點吃的吧。
The dog was grubbing around/about in the mud for a bone.
那隻狗在泥中刨來扒去找骨頭。

NONE: › to dig something out of the ground to get rid of it
（連根）掘出，挖出

example: She spent the morning in the garden, grubbing up weeds.
她花了一上午的時間在花園裡除草。

NONE: › informal dirty
（同 dirty）
› disapproving If you describe an activity or someone's behaviour as grubby, you do not think that it is honest, fair, or acceptable.
卑鄙的，可鄙的

example: He was wearing some old shorts and a grubby T-shirt.
他穿著一條破舊的短褲和一件髒兮兮的T恤衫。
Don't wipe your grubby hands on my clean towel!
別拿我的乾淨毛巾擦你那骯髒手！
She sees the business of making money as just grubby opportunism.
在她眼中，賺錢的生意只不過是可鄙的投機行為而已。
He doesn't want this story to get into the grubby hands of the tabloid press (= to be obtained by newspapers that are not honest and fair).
他不想讓這件事情登到那些卑鄙下流的小報上去。

NONE: › a strong feeling of anger and dislike for a person who you feel has treated you badly, especially one that lasts for a long time
怨恨，嫌隙，積怨
› also begrudge to not want to spend time or money on someone or something, or to not want to give something to someone
吝惜；勉強地做，勉強地給
› also begrudge to think that someone does not deserve something good that they have
認為…不應得到；忌妒

example: I don't bear any grudge against you.
我對你沒有絲毫怨恨。
Amanda still has/holds a grudge against me for refusing to lend her that money.
艾曼達到現在仍對我不借錢給她一事耿耿於懷。
She grudged every hour she spent helping him.
她很不情願花時間幫他。
[ + two objects ] I don't grudge you your holiday, it's just that you've chosen a bad time to go.
我不是認為你不該去度假，只是覺得你選的時機不合適。

NONE: › a sports game between people or teams who dislike each other or are unhappy about the result of a previous game between them
（體育競賽中）雙方都不喜歡對方的比賽；雙方都對上一場比賽結果不滿的比賽
› A grudging action or feeling is one that you do or have unwillingly.
勉強的，不情願的

example: She won the grudging respect of her boss.
她的老闆也不由得敬重她。

NONE: › a cheap simple food made, especially in the past, by boiling oats with water or milk
（尤指舊時的）稀粥，燕麥粥
› extremely tiring and difficult, and demanding great effort and determination
使人精疲力盡的；艱辛的；讓人受不了的

example: Junior doctors often have to work a gruelling 100-hour week.
資歷較淺的醫生經常必須承受艱巨的工作量，一星期工作100小時。
He eventually won the match after five gruelling sets.
經過五局艱難的拼殺，他終於贏得了比賽。

NONE: › extremely unpleasant and shocking, and usually dealing with death or injury
（通常用來描述死亡或者傷害）令人厭惡的，恐怖的，可怕的

example: The newspaper article included a gruesome description of the murder.
這篇報導中有一段對謀殺案血淋淋的描述。

NONE: › (of a person's voice) low and unfriendly, or (of a person's behaviour) unfriendly or showing no patience
（聲音）低沉而生硬的，粗聲粗氣的；（行為）不友好的，不耐煩的，粗暴的

example: "Yeah, so what?" came the gruff reply.
「是的，那又怎樣？」對方生硬地回答道。
He's quite a sweet man beneath the gruff exterior.
他外表冷漠內心善良。

NONE: › to complain about someone or something in an annoyed way
發牢騷，抱怨，嘟囔
› If your stomach grumbles, it makes a low, continuous noise, usually because you are hungry.
（通常因為餓而）肚子咕咕叫
› a complaint
（同 complaint）

example: She spent the evening grumbling to me about her job.
她整晚都在向我抱怨她的工作。
[ + speech ] "You never hang your coat up," she grumbled.
「你就從來不會把外套掛起來。」她埋怨道。
When the teacher assigned extra homework, she heard a few grumbles from the kids.
要是再讓我聽到你抱怨飯不好吃，你就自己做！

NONE: › a medical condition in which the appendix (= the tube-shaped part that is joined to the intestines) causes you slight pain over a period of time
闌尾陣痛（指闌尾持續輕微疼痛但未形成闌尾炎）
› someone who is easily annoyed and complains a lot
脾氣壞的人；愛抱怨的人

example: He's only an old grump - don't listen to him.
他就是那種壞脾氣——別理他。

NONE: C1 easily annoyed and complaining
脾氣壞的，易生氣的；愛抱怨的

example: I hadn't had enough sleep and was feeling kind of grumpy.
我睡眠不足，所以感到有點煩躁。
a grumpy old man
脾氣不好的老人

NONE: › a type of rock music and a fashion for untidy clothes, popular in the early 1990s
（流行於20世紀90年代初的）頹廢音樂，格郎基音樂；（20世紀90年代初期年輕人以穿著邋遢為時尚的）格郎基風尚，頹廢風尚

example: Nirvana was one of the most famous grunge bands.
「涅磐」是最著名的頹廢音樂樂隊之一。

NONE: › (of a person) feeling tired and dirty, or (of a thing) dirty
（人）無精打采的，邋遢的；（物）骯髒的

example: He showed up for the interview wearing some grungy old sweatshirt and jeans.
面試時，他身穿又髒又破的長袖運動衫和牛仔褲出現在大家面前。

NONE: › (of a pig) to make a low, rough noise
（豬）發出呼嚕聲
› (of a person) to make a short, low sound instead of speaking, usually because of anger or pain
（人通常因為憤怒或疼痛而）發出哼聲，嘟囔著說，咕噥

example: The pigs were grunting contentedly as they ate their food.
豬邊吃邊發出滿意的哼哼聲。
He hauled himself over the wall, grunting with the effort.
他費力地翻過牆，累得直哼哼。
[ + speech ] "Too tired," he grunted and sat down.
「累死了。」他呻吟著坐下來。

NONE: › happy or satisfied
高興的；滿意的

example: Although he wasn't actually disgruntled, he was far from being gruntled.
儘管他並不是不滿意，但也遠遠談不上滿意。

NONE: › a hard, pale yellow, strong-tasting cheese that is made in Switzerland
（原產於瑞士的）格魯耶爾起司
